description: S458 / S478: the runtime check tests the BASE type before the predicate. take(n: number(>0)) is called with the number 7 (passes; @shown becomes 7), then with a value from a SERVER ANSWER the typer cannot see: loadAmount() is declared `-> number`, but its answer is stubbed as the STRING "9". That value is refused before take's body runs (E-CONTRACT-001-RT, §53.3.4 — or, on an implementation that decodes the wire strictly (§57), the answer is refused at the wire and the handler's fallback `0` fails the predicate), so @shown keeps 7. Before S458 the check was `(n > 0)`, which JavaScript coerces: "9" > 0 is true, so a string inhabited `number(>0)`.
rationale: §53.3.4: "A `number(>0 && <10000)` value IS a `number`. The constrained type is a subtype of the base type" — a value that is not of the base type cannot inhabit the refinement; §53.4.5 the boundary check refuses it. S478 open-Qs ruling (user-voice) item 25: the case was rewritten so the typer cannot see the non-number (it arrives in a server answer) — before, it passed a `string` cell straight to the `number(>0)` parameter, which §7.3.4 / §7.5.1 position 3 (S447 call 9) make a compile-time E-TYPE-031, so the runtime check was not what refused it.
